## Video 1 — `affordance_drag_hover_shadows`

### What is visibly present

- **WEBSITE work:** The video begins with D&D Beyond’s own loading screen and then the plain “Corvo Saggio” character sheet. The D&D Beyond navigation bar, character statistics, actions, inventory, conditions, and other sheet content are website product.
- **EXTENSION work:** Around 26.8 seconds, two distinct dark floating panels appear:
  - A left control panel with **LAYOUT**, **OUTPUT**, **PROPERTIES**, and **CANVAS FILTERS** sections.
  - A right **LAYER MANAGEMENT** panel listing sections and shapes.
- **EXTENSION work:** The panels use a black/dark “codex” treatment with gold accents and are clearly distinguishable from D&D Beyond’s own UI.
- **EXTENSION work:** A centered toast reports **“No saved layout yet — the default template is loaded.”**
- **EXTENSION work:** A later toast reports **“Shape Default Hidden.”** The corresponding shape disappears from the Layer Management shape area.
- **EXTENSION work:** Small dark action clusters appear near hovered sheet elements. These are extension-provided section actions rather than website controls.
- The page is scrolled during the sequence, revealing more of the enhanced sheet. The scrolling itself is not evidence of a drag implementation.

### Layer 1 — Asserted-behavior evidence

| Suite assertion | Camera evidence |
|---|---|
| The green hover glow no longer paints on a hovered, draggable section. | **NOT-VISIBLE** — no clearly sampled hovered section with enough detail to verify the absence of a green glow. |
| Every section wrapper carries ONE nine-dot handle in its rail’s first slot, hidden and unhittable at rest. | **NOT-VISIBLE** — no nine-dot handle is clearly identifiable, and rest-state hittability cannot be tested visually. |
| Hovering the ACTIVE layer reveals the handle in the rail’s first slot, grabbable, with no glow. | **NOT-VISIBLE** — extension action clusters are visible, but a nine-dot active-layer handle is not clearly shown or grabbed. |
| With the decorative layer hidden through its own control, every revealed grip is grabbable. | **NOT-VISIBLE** — hiding the shape is visible, but the revealed grips are not clearly shown being grabbed. |
| An INACTIVE (locked) layer’s section reveals no handle even while hovered. | **NOT-VISIBLE** — no locked-layer hover is clearly sampled. |
| A section can really be DRAGGED from the handle, and a click on it does not move it. | **NOT-VISIBLE** — no handle-origin drag or click-vs-drag comparison is visibly demonstrated. |
| A section hue shift does not travel into the handle’s own chrome. | **NOT-VISIBLE** — no hue change plus handle-chrome comparison is visible. |
| Hovering the ACTIVE layer reveals `.be-section-actions` visible and clickable. | **VISIBLE** — dark extension action clusters are repeatedly revealed near hovered sections. The frames do not prove every control’s click result, but the action affordance itself is visible. |

### Layer 2 — Product-aim conformance

**Working affordances observed:**

- Extension panels appear cleanly and are visually distinct from the website.
- The left control panel exposes clear grouped navigation and recognizable controls such as **PRINT**, **Load**, **Reset to Default**, **Manage Clones**, and **Add Shape**.
- The Layer Management panel clearly separates **SECTIONS** and **SHAPES**, with visible counts and individual item names.
- The **“No saved layout yet — the default template is loaded.”** toast gives useful state feedback.
- **“Shape Default Hidden”** confirms that a shape visibility operation produces visible feedback and changes the shape layer’s displayed state.
- Hovered elements reveal compact dark action controls in the extension’s visual language.
- The extension maintains a coherent dark-and-gold visual identity rather than imitating D&D Beyond’s controls.

**Missing or rough affordances observed:**

- The central nine-dot drag grip is not clearly visible, so the most important drag affordance cannot be evaluated on camera.
- No clear visual distinction is shown between an active layer and a locked/inactive layer.
- No clearly demonstrated mouse drag commits a section to a new position.
- No visible click-versus-drag behavior is demonstrated.
- No alignment guides or live snap are shown in this video.
- No post-drag **“Layout saved”** toast is visible.
- No error state or drag rejection message is shown.
- The browser toolbar and its claimed ON badge are outside the captured viewport.
- The first-run hint card described by the product is not visible.
- Disabled controls are present in the panel, but no on-camera interaction demonstrates what happens when an unavailable action is selected.

**Video verdict:** **PARTIAL** — the extension UI and several hover/visibility affordances are visible, but the central drag-handle behaviors are not adequately witnessed.

## Video 2 — `drag_glow_layers`

### What is visibly present

- **WEBSITE work:** The video opens with D&D Beyond’s loading screen and then the plain character sheet.
- **EXTENSION work:** The left control panel and the right Layer Management panel appear around 27 seconds.
- **EXTENSION work:** The toast **“No saved layout yet — the default template is loaded.”** appears above the enhanced sheet.
- The enhanced sheet shows the extension’s section borders and reorganized/resizable section presentation.
- The Layer Management panel lists 22 sections and one shape, with individual section names and visibility controls.
- No sustained hover, pointer drag, touch drag, click, panel minimize, or restore interaction is visibly demonstrated before the recording ends.

### Layer 1 — Asserted-behavior evidence

| Suite assertion | Camera evidence |
|---|---|
| Sections and shapes are headerless wrappers titled via `data-title`. | **NOT-VISIBLE** — headerless appearance may be suggested by the sheet, but the `data-title` attribute and wrapper structure cannot be verified visually. |
| Pointer drags arm on the wrapper background but not on action bars or buttons. | **NOT-VISIBLE** — no pointer drag or armed/non-armed comparison is shown. |
| Locked layers are interaction-safe (styled locked + never armed for drag). | **NOT-VISIBLE** — no locked layer is clearly selected or hovered. |
| Hover and active glow highlight styles are injected (and print strips them). | **NOT-VISIBLE** — no clear hover/active glow comparison or print output is shown. |
| Layer Management panel minimizes and restores. | **NOT-VISIBLE** — the panel is visible, but no minimize or restore operation is shown. |

### Layer 2 — Product-aim conformance

**Working affordances observed:**

- The extension activates over the plain website sheet without replacing or obscuring the entire character sheet.
- Its control panel and Layer Management panel are immediately recognizable as separate extension products.
- The dark panels, gold trim, uppercase section labels, and compact icon controls form a coherent “codex on the workbench” design.
- The default-layout toast clearly communicates the initialized state.
- Section and shape counts are visible, providing useful management information.
- The section list and shape picker remain visually separate from the underlying D&D Beyond content.

**Missing or rough affordances observed:**

- The Layer Management panel’s minimize/restore behavior is not demonstrated.
- No explicit locked/active/inactive visual state is clearly demonstrated.
- No section action bar is visibly exercised.
- No pointer drag is shown, so the main feature family is largely absent from the camera evidence.
- No hover glow or active glow can be evaluated.
- No print-preview evidence shows that interaction styling is removed for printing.
- No error state, disabled-state explanation, or failed-drag feedback is visible.
- No autosave/save-success toast is shown.
- The browser toolbar icon and ON badge are not included in the recording.

**Video verdict:** **PARTIAL** — the extension’s activation and visual identity are visible, but the asserted drag-glow and layer-safety behaviors are not witnessed.

## Video 3 — `drag_ux_visual_capture`

### What is visibly present

- **WEBSITE work:** The sequence starts with the D&D Beyond loader and then the plain character sheet.
- **EXTENSION work:** The two extension panels appear around 27 seconds, with the same dark, gold-accented design.
- **EXTENSION work:** The **“No saved layout yet — the default template is loaded.”** toast is visible.
- **EXTENSION work:** The enhanced sheet is visibly reorganized into extension-managed boxes with themed borders and decorative artwork.
- The page scrolls up and down to reveal different portions of the enhanced sheet.
- Small extension action clusters are occasionally visible near sheet sections.
- No unmistakable custom drag ghost, touch gesture, gold alignment guide, locked-layer presentation, or post-drop save toast is sampled.

### Layer 1 — Asserted-behavior evidence

| Suite assertion | Camera evidence |
|---|---|
| Captures the sheet layout and a wrapper rest/hover state. | **VISIBLE** — the enhanced sheet layout is clearly captured, and extension hover/action affordances appear on some sections. |
| Captures a committed pointer drag with the custom ghost (mouse). | **NOT-VISIBLE** — no unmistakable mouse drag or custom ghost is shown. |
| Captures the same-session before/after pair (source restored, wrapper moved). | **NOT-VISIBLE** — no clear source-restoration and wrapper-movement pair is presented. |
| Captures a touch-pointer drag mid-gesture (`pointerType: touch`). | **NOT-VISIBLE** — no touch-pointer gesture is shown. |
| Captures a live-snapped drag with gold alignment guides and the zero-jump drop. | **NOT-VISIBLE** — no alignment guides or snapped drop are visible. |
| Captures the locked-layer state (no drag affordance, dimmed). | **NOT-VISIBLE** — no clear locked/dimmed state is shown. |
| Captures the post-drop autosave toast after release. | **NOT-VISIBLE** — the only toast is the default-layout notice; no post-drop autosave toast is shown. |
| Captures a drop clamped to the sheet origin (never negative). | **NOT-VISIBLE** — no clamped drop is shown. |

### Layer 2 — Product-aim conformance

**Working affordances observed:**

- The extension activates from the plain sheet to a substantially enhanced presentation.
- The floating control panel and Layer Management panel are clearly extension-specific and visually unlike D&D Beyond.
- The enhanced sheet uses extension-provided section boxes, borders, themed decoration, and a more codex-like composition.
- The default-layout notification provides an initialization state.
- Section action clusters appear on hover.
- The extension remains available while the user scrolls through a long sheet.
- The panel hierarchy and labels are generally understandable and visually consistent.

**Missing or rough affordances observed:**

- The expected custom drag ghost is absent from the sampled frames.
- No mouse drag is visibly committed.
- No touch drag is shown.
- No live-snap guide or zero-jump drop is shown.
- No before/after drag pair demonstrates that the source is restored.
- No locked-layer visual state is shown.
- No autosave/save toast appears after a drop.
- No negative-coordinate/clamping behavior is demonstrated.
- No drag error, rejection, or boundary-state message is shown.
- The “SAVE” affordance is visible in the Layer Management header, but no save operation or resulting state is demonstrated.
- No browser toolbar badge is visible.
- The panels remain fixed while the sheet scrolls, which is visually coherent, but no responsive/minimized behavior is demonstrated.

**Video verdict:** **PARTIAL** — the enhanced layout and panel system are well represented, but most of the visual drag-capture contract is not witnessed.

---

## Overall assessment

The extension’s strongest on-camera result is its clear visual separation from D&D Beyond: the floating dark control panel, Layer Management panel, themed sheet enhancement, section-action clusters, and state toasts are unmistakably extension work. The off state and activation transition are also represented.

However, none of the videos provides sufficient visual evidence for the central nine-dot drag handle, active-versus-locked layer semantics, custom pointer/touch drag ghosts, alignment-guide snapping, source restoration, clamping, or post-drop autosave. The missing behavior is extensive enough that a **WORKING** verdict is not supportable, but the frames are not too sparse or blank to justify an overall **NOT-VISIBLE** verdict.

VERDICT: PARTIAL
